newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Capitals of Taiwan, Mongolia become sister cities.
newsitem.headline: Capitals of Taiwan, Mongolia become sister cities.

text.p: Taiwan's opposition-ruled capital Taipei on Friday forged sister-city ties with Mongolia's capital Ulan Bator -- in effect renouncing the Nationalist government's claim of sovereignty over Mongolia.

The exiled Republic of China government, which took refuge on Taiwan after its 1949 civil war defeat to the communists, has never abandoned its claim to the Chinese mainland -- and maintains that China still includes Mongolia.
Establishing the sister-city link accords with the Taipei municipal government's view that Taiwan is independent of China and that its claims of sovereignty over Mongolia are invalid.

"We are using our action to rewrite history and create new history," Taipei mayor Chen Shui-bian, a leader of the independence-minded opposition Democratic Progressive Party, said during a ceremony allying the two cities.
Sister city relationships typically are formed between foreign cities, not those in the same country.

Mongolia was allied with China during the 1644-1911 Qing dynasty. It embraced communism in 1921 and allied itself with the Soviet Union, existing as a quasi-independent vassal of Moscow until the Soviet collapse enabled Mongolia to embrace multiparty democracy in the early 1990s.
Controversy over the exiled Chinese republic's claim to Mongolia still vexes Taiwan.

Taiwan President and Nationalist Party chairman Lee Teng-hui in April rejected an opposition proposal that would have scrapped a panel set up in the 1950s to bolster Taiwan's claims of sovereignty over Mongolia and Tibet.
Taiwan school textbooks, standardised by the government's education ministry, all refer to Mongolia as part of China.
